Generated by `python -m prahari.research paper` from the committed result files; every number below is in
[numbers.md](../numbers.md) under the key shown in brackets. **SIM** = simulator output; **REAL** = public data.
Bullet points only: the authors write the paper's prose (charter rule 10). The claim and title are the

map says so.

## Contribution 1 — a pre-registered, equal-false-alarm evaluation on an open, deterministic testbed

- **Status: supported** (method).
- Four registered rounds (R1–R4) and a registered real-data plan; protocol commits precede every result file;
  one seed per round regenerates byte for byte ([audit-2026-10-07.md](../audit-2026-10-07.md) §1).
- SIM, R1 family A at 10 false incidents a month: P2 confirms 83.3% of fires within 3 h [`test.P2.at_budget.10.det`];
  differences +36.8, +51.6, +32.6 points against P0 fixed threshold, P1t v1 replay-tuned, AR(1) residual chart, Holm p ≤ 1.2e-15; P1 v1 as written cannot reach the budget [`comparisons.10.A.*`].
- SIM, the textbook ARL threshold: 123.9–170.5 false incidents a month at every sweep point [`sweeps.<point>.pipelines.P1.fa_at_first_knob`].
- Figure: `f2_operating_curves`. Table: T2 (R1 rows).
- Caveat: absolute detection is plume-conditional (P2 at 10 a month: 84.5% with the legacy plume, 35.9% with the Gaussian plume, R1 sweep seeds) [`sweeps.plume=real.pipelines.P2`].

## Contribution 2 — the decomposition: node calibration meets its budget; regional smoke sets the floor

- **(a) Node calibration meets its budget — supported.**
  - REAL, quiet N5 networks: 0.00–1.69 node candidates per node per 30 d against a target of 1 (configuration); exceedance 0.4%–1.6% at a nominal 1% [`clusters.<BC|VC|RC>.node_replay`].
  - REAL, Delhi smoke season (DL15, 15 min): 1.41 per node per 30 d; 3.1% of candidates in common mode [`clusters.DL15-2025.node_replay`].
- **(b) "Regional smoke sets a floor that node thresholds cannot move" — not supported as an unmovable floor;**
  **supported in a revised form.**
  - SIM: R1's floor (5.07 a month [`test.P2.curve`]) belonged to SCMR's fixed ratio ρ = 3. With ρ free, P2's lowest rate is 0.22–1.28 a month across R2 and R3 [audit rows "lowest false incidents/month at ρ = 3 vs at any ρ"].
  - SIM: what remains is smoke: 83.5%–100.0% of P2's floor incidents start inside haze (R1–R3) [`split.P2.inside_share`, `…floor_at_selected_knob.decomposition.share_inside`].
  - SIM, R4 family P (confirmatory): at 1 false incident a month, detection without haze minus with haze is +22.1, +37.2, +36.0 points (P2, median + SCMR, gate), Holm p ≤ 1.2e-17 [`family_P[*]`].
  - SIM, R4: useful floors 0.00–0.07 a month without haze against 0.85–1.42 with haze [`scenarios[*].floors[*]`].
  - SIM, R4: with haze, the stricter node targets (0.03 and 0.05) leave every useful-floor setting unchanged; without haze, the useful floors are 0.00–0.11 a month with or without them [`selection.H-mix.methods.*[useful_floor*]`, `scenarios[H-none].floors[*][useful_floor*]`].
  - Candidate revised claim, for the developer to decide and the authors to word: smoke sets the detection
    price of strict false-alarm budgets, and stricter node thresholds did not lower the useful floor with haze (R4).
- Figures: `r4_price`, `r4_dose`, `r4_floors`, `paper_realdata` (a). Tables: T2 (R4 rows), T3.
- Caveats: SIM; H-mix's haze rate is a stress setting next to the real rates (contribution 4); SCMR's ratio
  cannot exceed N divided by the neighbourhood size (100/9 for interior clusters, DER), so floors are conditional
  on the network geometry.

## Contribution 3 — common-mode strategies under synchronous and uneven haze, and where each breaks

- **Status: supported.**
  - SIM, R1 (synchronous haze): median subtraction confirms 92.1% at 10 a month, +8.8 points over P2 at ρ = 3 [`test.P2-med.at_budget.10.det`, `comparisons.10.B.P2-med`].
  - SIM, R2 (uneven haze): median subtraction fails — floor 4.22 a month, 62.5% at B* = 10 (family D -28.2 points, Holm p 5.4e-17) [`scenarios.H-mix.methods.P2-med`, `…families.D.P2-med`].
  - SIM, R2: among the valid methods, median + SCMR detects most at B* (92.2%); median + SCMR − P2 +1.8 points (Holm p 0.00026); the gate has the lowest floor (0.16 a month; family F -0.40 a month) at a near-silent setting (1.7% detection); Mei's network sum cannot hold any budget (R2-D1).
  - SIM, R3 (head to head, B* = 1): H1 -8.7 points (median + SCMR − gate, Holm p 0.012); H2 +0.45 false incidents a month (Holm p 0.00028); the ranking changes with the budget [`scenarios.H-mix.head_to_head`].
  - SIM, R4 (descriptive): with haze at 1 a month, P2 − median + SCMR +13.3 points and P2 − gate +13.9 points; R3's H1 is not repeated (median + SCMR − gate +0.6 points, p 0.58) [`scenarios[H-mix].method_differences[1]`].
- Figures: `paper_strategies`, `r2_floor_H-mix`. Table: T2 (R2, R3 rows).
- Caveats: which haze scenario is realistic for a MOX network is open (real events are mostly more even than M20b);
  at ρ = 10, SCMR confirms an interior cluster only while the rest of the network is quiet.

## Contribution 4 — real-data checks of common-mode events and of the node layer's quiet false-alarm rate

- **Status: supported for the premises; the floor's size cannot be measured on real data.**
  - REAL: node calibration as in contribution 2 (a); near recorded fires (N5 WR) the node layer raised 6.38 candidates per node per 30 d, 70.6% of them in common mode — at kilometre spacing a fire's own smoke looks common-mode [`clusters.WR.node_replay`].
  - REAL, NW India: network-wide events are rarer than the simulator's H-mix rate (pooled per cluster: ×0.05–×0.31) and mostly more even across stations than M20b's draws [`pooled.*`, `clusters.*.held_out`].
  - REAL: Stuttgart (urban PM, 9 sensors): 0.226 events per day [`cluster.events_per_day`].
- Figure: `paper_realdata`. Table: T3.
- Caveats: PM₂.₅ and CO, not MOX; kilometre to regional spacing; 0–7 events per network or cluster-year (descriptive only) [`clusters.*.n_events`, `cluster.n_events`, `clusters.*.held_out`]; DL15's
  licence is not listed by OpenAQ (the developer's decision, DECISIONS P-9); Aakash data are CC BY-NC-ND (no
  redistribution).

## Claims to avoid

- "First" or "no one else", unless the authors verify it against the literature.
- "N× fewer false alarms" at unequal detection; every comparison here is at equal false alarms.
- Field performance, real-world lead time, or a conformal guarantee under autocorrelation.
- An unmovable floor (the title's strong form): with ρ free, P2's floor is 0.22–1.28 a month (contribution 2).
- R3's H1 as a general advantage of the gate: R4 does not repeat it.
- Mei's registered R2 advantage: it is the continuous-alarm artefact (R2-D1).
- That the risk-adaptive quorum beats a fixed quorum: in R1 it does not beat a fixed quorum of 3.
- Absolute detection independent of the plume model (contribution 1 caveat).

## Open decisions

- **The developer:** the claim and title (contribution 2 (b)); the venue; the release tag and DOI.
- **The authors:** the novelty check against the literature; every reference read before citing; the similarity
  check; the AI disclosure (IEEE policy).
